It\\u0026#39;s not in my app code. (Answer follows)\\n\\nThird, where are these script tags getting injected? They are not in the initial HTML being served to the browser.\\n\\nThe answer to the second and third puzzles is *identity server\\u0026#39;s `/connect/checksession` endpoint*. If you look at the network trace for it:\\n\\n![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1101362/136238297-74e61316-bdb6-4a7d-b5c1-db8dcd761ecf.png)\\n\\nPlus the response headers contain:\\n\\n```\\ncontent-security-policy: default-src \\u0026#39;none\\u0026#39;; script-src \\u0026#39;sha256-fa5rxHhZ799izGRP38+h4ud5QXNT0SFaFlh4eqDumBI=\\u0026#39;\\n```\\n\\n**I\\u0026#39;m pretty sure this cannot be a valid place for us to inject either the Browserlink script or the `aspnetcore-browser-refresh.js` script**, because:\\n\\n1. Why would we do this? Then they only take effect when you\\u0026#39;re logged in. That can\\u0026#39;t be what we want. Also I think they would incorrectly try to reload whatever hidden iframe this file is being loaded into, and who knows what that will lead to.\\n2. The CSP is going to deny them anyway.\\n\\nI\\u0026#39;m not really certain whether either Browserlink or ASP.NET Core hot reload should be present in the SPA templates. Maybe not, in which case somehow removing them would fix all of this. But if they are meant to be there we need to find a different way to inject them.\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"locked\":true,\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/37326\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"SteveSandersonMS\",\"id\":1101362,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/SteveSandersonMS\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1101362?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"MEMBER\",\"labels\":[\"area-mvc\",\"feature-spa\"],\"assignees\":[\"pranavkm\",\"jodavis\"],\"milestone\":\"6.0.0\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2021-10-06T15:50:46Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2021-11-11T18:00:41Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2021-10-12T17:02:29Z\",\"closed_by\":\"pranavkm\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

A brand new app used to trip over that on its own navigation menu, so the very first thing such a team did was work around the template. This validates that an app created from the template works under a strict policy without that concession, and that its navigation menu still behaves.\\n\\n## Minimum build\\n\\n.NET 11 Preview 7 or later.\\n\\n## Configurations to cover\\n\\n* Blazor Web App\\n  * [x] Static SSR\\n  * [x] Interactive Server\\n  * [x] Interactive WebAssembly\\n  * [x] Interactive Auto\\n* [ ] Standalone WebAssembly\\n* [ ] Hybrid (MAUI)\\n\\n## Also exercise\\n\\n* [x] Published output\\n* [ ] An existing .NET 10 app upgraded to .NET 11\\n* [ ] Trimming or ahead-of-time compilation\\n* [ ] More than one server instance, or a proxy in front\\n* [ ] Hot Reload\\n* [ ] An IDE as well as the command line\\n* [ ] Container\\n\\n## Setup\\n\\nNothing beyond the shared instructions, but you will be adding a strict Content Security Policy to the app yourself as part of the exercise.\\n\\n## What to build\\n\\nCreate an app from the template with the sample content included, and confirm it works as it stands. Then apply a strict Content Security Policy that forbids scripts embedded in the page, without granting any exception for the app\\u0026#39;s own inline scripts, and without `unsafe-inline` or `unsafe-hashes` in `script-src`. Then use the app on a narrow window or a phone-sized viewport, where the navigation menu collapses and has to be opened and closed.\\n\\n## Things to try\\n\\n* Using the app before applying the policy, so you know what correct looks like.\\n* Applying the policy and reloading, watching the browser console for anything the policy blocked.\\n* Starting in report-only mode to collect violations without breaking the app, then switching to enforcing.\\n* Narrowing the window until the navigation menu collapses, then opening and closing it.\\n* Opening the menu and choosing a page from it.\\n* Opening the menu, then tapping outside it.\\n* Moving between pages and then using the menu again, without a full reload.\\n* Resizing the window back and forth across the point where the menu collapses.\\n\\n## Expected behavior\\n\\nThe app runs under a strict policy that forbids scripts embedded in the page, and the browser console reports nothing blocked. The navigation menu opens, closes and navigates on narrow viewports exactly as it does without the policy, including after moving between pages. Nothing in the template requires a per-app exception to be added to the policy for its own scripts.\\n\\n### Must hold\\n\\n* With the policy applied and no exception granted for inline scripts, the browser console reports nothing blocked.\\n* On a narrow viewport the navigation menu opens, closes, and navigates to a chosen page.\\n* The menu still works after moving between pages without a full reload.\\n* Nothing in the template requires a per-app inline script exception to be added to the policy.\\n\\n### Expected differences between configurations\\n\\n* No differences are expected.\\n\\n## Documentation to use\\n\\nThe new behavior is built into the project template, so there is no .NET 11 documentation to follow for the feature itself. Create a new default Blazor Web App.\\n2. Select any render mode:\\n\\u0026gt; - Static SSR\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Server\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive WebAssembly\\n\\u0026gt; - Interactive Auto\\n4. Not observed in Google Chrome.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNo application exceptions are thrown.\\n\\nBrowser console output: `Permissions policy violation: unload is not allowed in this document`\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n11.0.100-preview.7.26381.103\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n**Environment**\\n\\n- VS 2026 Insiders [12023.133] professional\\n- Microsoft Edge\\n- Local Debug configuration\\n\\n**Additional Context**\\n\\nThe issue was discovered while validating CSP scenarios, but the behavior reproduces even when CSP is completely disabled, suggesting Browser Link or Visual Studio debugging integration as the source of the console violation rather than ASP.NET Core application code.\\n\\n**Repro Repository**\\n\\nSample App: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main\\nEvidence: https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693/BlazorCspValidation/tree/main/Evidence\",\"state\":\"closed\",\"state_reason\":\"completed\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/68678\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"BharatRamsf3693\",\"id\":103921986,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/BharatRamsf3693\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/103921986?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"CONTRIBUTOR\",\"labels\":[\"External\"],\"comments\":2,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2026-08-21T07:02:08Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:24Z\",\"closed_at\":\"2026-08-26T06:56:11Z\",\"closed_by\":\"danroth27\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

(it is triggered by the `@attribute [Authorize(Policy = \\u0026#34;Root\\u0026#34;)]` on the razor page)\\n\\nWhen a client lose connection with the server, the overlay `Attempting to reconnect to the server: N of M` appears:\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/3bc90594-35bc-4c18-b38e-36d049c2c170)\\n\\nWhen the client gains back the connection with the server, the same `Circuit` is maintained successfully and the authorization is validated again.\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is very fast, the component will resume with its state successfully: \\n\\n![msedge_qx0mIIpW8p](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/725966b5-9cdc-4a73-ad34-4b031bb413b7)\\n\\nWhen the process of the `IAuthorizationHandler` is taking too \\u0026#34;long\\u0026#34;, the component will be unloaded, replaced with `Authorizing...` when reconnecting, then after authorization is successful, the component will be reloaded with a brand new state, which leads to losing the data that was on the page before losing connection with the server.\\n\\n![msedge_HSVumEpB7Y](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/22667054/25800601-c24c-4058-b5da-76ac325434dd)\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nIn my opinion, there is multiple expected behavior:\\n\\n- The `Authorizing...` should appear but the other component should keep its state while it is pending for authorization.\\n- The user should be able to prevent the `Authorizing...` from appearing. (Is it not possible already?)\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n1. Configure a simple policy `Root` with a custom requirement\\n2. Implement a `IAuthorizationHandler` with a huge delay on it that `Succeed` your pending custom requirement\\n3. Open your DevTools on your browser \\n4. Open a razor page that has a `@attribute [Authorize(Policy = \\u0026#34;Root\\u0026#34;)]`\\n5. Go offline from your DevTools to lose connection with Blazor Server\\n6. Wait for the \\u0026#34;Attempting to reconnect to the server...\\u0026#34;\\n7. Go online again from your DevTools to make SignalR reconnect successfully to Blazor Server\\n\\nAnd now, with a big delay, you should see the component disappear, having `Authorizing...` appear, then the component reloading with its default state.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\nNo exceptions.\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n8.0.100-rc.1.23455.8\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nMicrosoft Visual Studio When navigating to `/error`, the Error page is rendered statically on the server, then when the client app starts, overwrites the Error page with the NotFound page content on the client. \\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nThe default project should demonstrate how to mix server-rendered and client-rendered content properly in the same app. Currently, the default project itself demonstrates mixing the render modes incorrectly.\\n\\nWhile putting `@attribute [ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting]` can be considered a workaround, it is undesirable: the layout of the application itself might still be using WebAssembly for even simple interactivity, like collapsing menus. `ExcludeFromInteractiveRouting` bypasses starting the WebAssembly runtime altogether.\\n\\nPossible solutions:\\n- Mark server-rendered content to persist on the client after client interactive routing kicks in. Possibly a marker attribute on the element, a directive, or an `@attribute` similar to `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute`.\\n- Allow `ExcludeFromInteractiveRoutingAttribute` to actually initialize the WebAssembly app, but leave the components marked with this attribute as-is in the DOM. Consider renaming the attribute if so. This might be easy to do using similar mechanics as seen in `PersistentState`\\n- Allow customizing the `Router`. For example, allow a behavior that lets the router \\u0026#34;keep\\u0026#34; the content as-is when a navigation event occurs, by overriding/passing `OnNavigatingAsync` or similar, or by inheriting from the built-in `Router`.\\n- Allow supplying a custom `Router` altogether. This would also allow multiple additional scenarios if community-built routers were to show up: handling localization in the URL, multiple hierarchic routers, etc.\\n- Allow rendering content on the server and let the client WebAssembly app \\u0026#34;consume\\u0026#34; the rendered static HTML as interactive. This might be a stretch, but for some simple cases, it can work.\\n- Modify/implement a new `RenderMode` that allows server-client handoff.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\n`dotnet new blazor --name BlazorSSRCSR --all-interactive --interactivity WebAssembly`\\n`cd BlazorSSRCSR`\\n`dotnet run`\\n\\nNavigate to the created app\\u0026#39;s `/error` endpoint. The endpoint will show the server side error, then after a short time, the client side router overwrites the content with the client side `NotFound` page content.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n10.0.100-rc.1.25451.107\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\nThis is NOT the same as similar (possibly slightly related) issues:\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/38128\\n- https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/42561\\n\\nNote that there\\u0026#39;s also the implication that if this is done, \\u0026#34;mixing\\u0026#34; render modes across a hierarchy might become possible. That would also require the user be able to set `RenderMode` to `Static` explicitly, which is currently not possible because it\\u0026#39;s not even defined in `RenderMode`: it\\u0026#39;s condered `Static` rendering when the `RenderMode` evaluates to `null`.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/63842\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"yugabe\",\"id\":14803737,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/yugabe\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/14803737?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":6,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2025-09-26T13:34:52Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2026-02-13T11:20:42Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The `opener` is from another origin so most operation throws Permission Denied error and I only intend to use it for `postMessage`. However if I pass it to any JS function, Blazor attempts to call `Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty` on it and causes the app to crash. This also happens to `iframe`s.\\n\\n\\u0026gt; Blocked a frame with origin \\u0026#34;https://localhost:44357\\u0026#34; from accessing a cross-origin frame.\\n\\n![image](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/assets/6388546/969c3ec6-f21e-4d10-b414-0fe51d8aa37b)\\n\\n```js\\nglobalThis.wasmInterop = new class {\\n\\n    getOpener() {\\n        return globalThis.parent;\\n    }\\n\\n    sendReadyMessage(window, op) {\\n        window.postMessage({\\n            op,\\n        });\\n    }\\n\\n}();\\n```\\n\\n```cs\\n@inject IJSRuntime Js;\\n// ...\\n\\nIJSObjectReference? opener;\\n\\nprotected override async Task OnInitializedAsync()\\n{\\n    opener = await Js.InvokeAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.getOpener\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n\\nasync Task SendMessageAsync()\\n{\\n    ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(opener);\\n\\n    // This one is fine\\n    await opener.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;postMessage\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;, \\u0026#34;*\\u0026#34;);\\n\\n    // This one raises the error\\n    await Js.InvokeVoidAsync(\\u0026#34;wasmInterop.sendReadyMessage\\u0026#34;, opener, \\u0026#34;hello\\u0026#34;);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nInterestingly, invoking the reference directly doesn\\u0026#39;t cause a problem. It only happens when it is a function parameter. I traced the source code back to [this line in `ElementReferenceCapture.ts`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/Web.JS/src/Rendering/ElementReferenceCapture.ts#LL22C1-L22C1):\\n\\n```ts\\nDotNet.attachReviver((key, value) =\\u0026gt; {\\n  if (value \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; typeof value === \\u0026#39;object\\u0026#39; \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(value, elementRefKey) \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; typeof value[elementRefKey] === \\u0026#39;string\\u0026#39;) {\\n    return getElementByCaptureId(value[elementRefKey]);\\n  } else {\\n    return value;\\n  }\\n});\\n```\\n\\n### Expected Behavior\\n\\nIdeally `hasOwnProperty` should not be called, or at least Exception should be handled.\\n\\n### Steps To Reproduce\\n\\nGithub repo for the above code: https://github.com/datvm/BlazorHasOwnPropertyBugDemo, you should run both website, the bug can be seen by running the ASP.NET Core website on the Index page, click \\u0026#34;Send message\\u0026#34; button in the iframe.\\n\\n### Exceptions (if any)\\n\\n_No response_\\n\\n### .NET Version\\n\\n7.0.302\\n\\n### Anything else?\\n\\n_No response_\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/48521\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"datvm\",\"id\":6388546,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/datvm\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/6388546?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-jsinterop\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":0,\"+1\":0,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2023-05-30T18:27:34Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-13T15:30:27Z\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The return url needs to have the same origin as the current page.\",\"body\":\"I host my blazor webassembly application in sub-directory - https://localhost:5000/myapp\\n\\nBase path is defined in index.html: ``\\n\\nI use identity server for authentication so there is link to authentication page from component NotLoggedIn.razor:\\n  `\\u003ca href=\\\"authentication/login?returnUrl=@Uri.EscapeDataString(Navigation.Uri)\\\" rel=\\\"nofollow noreferrer\\\"\\u003elog in\\u003c/a\\u003e`\\n\\nand authentication page\\n```\\n@page \\u0026#34;/authentication/{action}\\u0026#34;\\n\\n\\n  ...\\n\\n\\n@code{\\n    [Parameter] public string Action { get; set; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nWhen I navigate to https://localhost:5000/myapp/ it works as expected.\\n\\nWhen I navigate to https://localhost:5000/myapp exception happens:\\n\\n\\u0026gt; Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Rendering.WebAssemblyRenderer[100]\\n\\u0026gt;       Unhandled exception rendering component: Invalid return url. The return url needs to have the same origin as the current page.\\n\\u0026gt; System.InvalidOperationException: Invalid return url. The return url needs to have the same origin as the current page.\\n\\u0026gt;   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication.RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore`1[TAuthenticationState].GetReturnUrl (TAuthenticationState state, System.String defaultReturnUrl) \\u0026lt;0x333cda8 + 0x00098\\u0026gt; in :0 \\n\\u0026gt;   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.WebAssembly.Authentication.RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore`1[TAuthenticationState].OnParametersSetAsync () \\u0026lt;0x333c238 + 0x001f0\\u0026gt; in :0 \\n\\u0026gt;   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase.CallStateHasChangedOnAsyncCompletion (System.Threading.Tasks.Task task) \\u0026lt;0x31b2bd8 + 0x000da\\u0026gt; in :0 \\n\\u0026gt;   at Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase.RunInitAndSetParametersAsync () \\u0026lt;0x2f63bf8 + 0x001d8\\u0026gt; in :0 \\n\\u0026gt; \\n\\nThis happens in method GetReturnUrl of RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore ln 346\\n\\n```\\n    private string GetReturnUrl(TAuthenticationState state, string defaultReturnUrl = null)\\n    {\\n        if (state?.ReturnUrl != null)\\n        {\\n            return state.ReturnUrl;\\n        }\\n\\n        var fromQuery = QueryStringHelper.GetParameter(new Uri(Navigation.Uri).Query, \\u0026#34;returnUrl\\u0026#34;);\\n        if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(fromQuery) \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp; !fromQuery.StartsWith(Navigation.BaseUri))\\n        {\\n            // This is an extra check to prevent open redirects.\\n            throw new InvalidOperationException(\\u0026#34;Invalid return url. The return url needs to have the same origin as the current page.\\u0026#34;);\\n        }\\n\\n        return fromQuery ?? defaultReturnUrl ?? Navigation.BaseUri;\\n    }\\n```\\n\\nBecause base path defined with slash on the end but current path doesn\\u0026#39;t contains slash the check: `!fromQuery.StartsWith(Navigation.BaseUri)` is true. \\n\\nUnfortunately I cannot define base w/o slash on the end because it breaks navigation.\\n\\n\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/24316\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"michaeldz\",\"id\":1072516,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/michaeldz\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/1072516?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"bug\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-few\",\"severity-major\",\"Priority:1\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"Pillar: Technical Debt\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":1,\"+1\":1,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":0,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":0,\"eyes\":0},\"created_at\":\"2020-07-25T23:02:30Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-02-05T06:59:09Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Bug\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

[2026-08-27T02:24:06.100Z] [DEBUG] [rpc] github←resp 5081b {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"result":{"_meta":{"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo":{"icons":[{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"light"},{"mimeType":"image/png","src":"data:image/png;base64,","theme":"dark"}],"name":"github-mcp-server","title":"GitHub MCP Server","version":"v1.9.0"}},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"{\"number\":25153,\"title\":\"Blazor WASM: RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore prevents use of ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath\",\"body\":\"I am building a Blazor WASM application that\\u0026#39;s connected to IdentityServer4.\\n\\nThe template for Single User Accounts provides ```LoginDisplay.razor``` which includes the following line:\\n\\n```\\n\\nAfter getting IdentityServer4 integrated via the following article, I noticed that the ```Register``` link simply redirected back to the Blazor app without any error messages.\\n\\nhttps://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/security/webassembly/hosted-with-identity-server?view=aspnetcore-3.1\\u0026amp;tabs=visual-studio\\n\\nIt wasn\\u0026#39;t clear what the ```RemoteAuthenticatorView``` was doing, so I dug into the code and came across the following:\\n\\nhttps://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/[REDACTED]/src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs#L356\\n\\nIt\\u0026#39;s clear that ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` is being used for the redirect, but there is no documentation describing this. After setting the value to my external identity site ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` (different site entirely), I was presented with ```Sorry, there\\u0026#39;s nothing at this address.``` in the Blazor app. \\n\\nLooking closer at the above line of code, the ```.PathAndQuery``` piece at the end prevents ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` from ever being outside the Blazor app.\\n\\nAs a result, setting ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteRegisterPath``` to ```https://localhost:44312/Identity/Account/Register``` executes a redirect to ```https://localhost:44357/Identity/Account/Register``` (my Blazor app).\\n\\nPlease confirm that this is a bug.\\n\\nEdit: ```ApplicationPaths.RemoteProfilePath``` seems to have the same issue.\",\"state\":\"open\",\"html_url\":\"https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/25153\",\"user\":{\"login\":\"hallidev\",\"id\":16142069,\"profile_url\":\"https://github.com/hallidev\",\"avatar_url\":\"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/16142069?v=4\"},\"author_association\":\"NONE\",\"labels\":[\"enhancement\",\"area-blazor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm\",\"affected-most\",\"severity-minor\",\"feature-blazor-wasm-auth\",\"triaged\",\"Pillar: Cloud Integration\"],\"milestone\":\"Backlog\",\"comments\":8,\"reactions\":{\"total_count\":17,\"+1\":9,\"-1\":0,\"laugh\":0,\"confused\":0,\"heart\":3,\"hooray\":0,\"rocket\":3,\"eyes\":2},\"created_at\":\"2020-08-22T17:46:27Z\",\"updated_at\":\"2025-08-26T13:02:51Z\",\"issue_type\":\"Feature\",\"has_parent\":false,\"has_children\":false,\"closed_by_pull_requests\":{\"total_count\":0,\"references\":[]}}"}],"resultType":"complete"}}

The complete authorization result, including `AuthorizationFailureReason` values, is discarded before rendering.\\n\\nThis prevents applications from displaying meaningful authorization failure messages in Blazor UI.\\n\\nThis proposal updates `AuthorizeViewCore` to preserve the full `AuthorizationResult` and expose authorization failure details through authorization-related template contexts.\\n\\nThe design adds:\\n\\n1. A new `AuthorizationStateWithResult` type that extends `AuthenticationState` and includes `AuthorizationResult`.\\n2. A new `Forbidden` render fragment for authenticated users who fail authorization.\\n3. Updated fallback behavior so `NotAuthorized` can receive an `AuthorizationStateWithResult` instance when authorization fails and `Forbidden` is not supplied.\\n\\nThis addresses both linked issues:\\n\\n- \\n- \\n\\n---\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nBlazor\\u0026#39;s `AuthorizeViewCore` currently evaluates authorization and renders one of the existing fragments:\\n\\n- `Authorizing`\\n- `Authorized`\\n- `ChildContent`\\n- `NotAuthorized`\\n\\nThe authorization result is reduced to a boolean value:\\n\\n```csharp\\nresult.Succeeded\\n```\\n\\nAs a result, metadata from `AuthorizationResult` is lost.\\n\\nThis is a problem because custom authorization handlers can produce useful failure reasons:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncontext.Fail(\\n    new AuthorizationFailureReason(\\n        this,\\n        \\u0026#34;Missing permission: Project.Read\\u0026#34;));\\n```\\n\\nToday, `AuthorizeView` does not provide a supported way for Razor markup to display that failure reason.\\n\\nThis creates two related gaps.\\n\\n### Gap 1: Authorization Result Is Not Exposed\\n\\nApplications cannot access the following from `AuthorizeView` UI templates:\\n\\n```csharp\\nAuthorizationResult\\nAuthorizationFailure\\nAuthorizationFailureReason\\n```\\n\\nThis prevents applications from showing detailed authorization failure messages.\\n\\n### Gap 2: Authenticated Forbidden Users Are Not Separated from Anonymous Users\\n\\nToday, both anonymous users and authenticated unauthorized users generally flow through `NotAuthorized`.\\n\\nApplications often need different UI:\\n\\n```text\\nAnonymous user:\\nPlease sign in.\\n\\nAuthenticated but unauthorized user:\\nYou are signed in, but you do not have permission.\\n```\\n\\nA dedicated `Forbidden` state gives applications a clearer way to represent the authenticated-but-not-authorized case.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Goals / Non-Goals\\n\\n### Goals\\n\\n1. Preserve the full `AuthorizationResult` returned by `IAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync`.\\n2. Expose authorization failure reasons to Blazor templates.\\n3. Add a dedicated `Forbidden` render fragment for authenticated-but-not-authorized users.\\n4. Preserve existing `NotAuthorized` source compatibility.\\n5. Allow `NotAuthorized` fallback scenarios to access authorization result information without changing the public `NotAuthorized` property type.\\n6. Preserve existing behavior when applications do not use the new API.\\n7. Keep the design simple for common Razor usage.\\n8. Avoid changing policy evaluation, role evaluation, resource authorization, or authentication behavior.\\n9. Provide a path that satisfies both scenarios: exposing the authorization result and separating forbidden UI from anonymous/not-authorized UI.\\n\\n### Non-Goals\\n\\n1. Do not change authorization policy semantics.\\n2. Do not change authentication behavior.\\n3. Do not remove or rename existing `AuthorizeView` parameters.\\n4. Do not require applications to use `Forbidden`.\\n5. Do not automatically sanitize, localize, or rewrite authorization failure messages.\\n6. Do not introduce a general-purpose diagnostics API for authorization.\\n7. Do not change routing authorization behavior outside the scope of `AuthorizeViewCore`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n## Detailed Design\\n\\n### Overview\\n\\nThe proposed design changes `AuthorizeViewCore` so that the component stores the full `AuthorizationResult` instead of only storing whether authorization succeeded.\\n\\nThe design introduces a new context type:\\n\\n```csharp\\nAuthorizationStateWithResult\\n```\\n\\nThis type derives from `AuthenticationState` and adds an `AuthorizationResult` property.\\n\\nThe same type is used by:\\n\\n1. `Forbidden`\\n2. `NotAuthorized` fallback scenarios where authorization failed\\n\\nThis design fixes both issues:\\n\\n- `Forbidden` provides a clear, explicit 403-style rendering path for authenticated users who fail authorization.\\n- `NotAuthorized` can still access authorization failure details when `Forbidden` is not supplied.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### New Context Type\\n\\nAdd a new public type:\\n\\n```csharp\\nnamespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization;\\n\\npublic sealed class AuthorizationStateWithResult : AuthenticationState\\n{\\n    public AuthorizationStateWithResult(\\n        ClaimsPrincipal user,\\n        AuthorizationResult authorizationResult)\\n        : base(user)\\n    {\\n        AuthorizationResult = authorizationResult;\\n    }\\n\\n    public AuthorizationResult AuthorizationResult { get; }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Purpose\\n\\n`AuthorizationStateWithResult` represents the current authentication state plus the result of authorization evaluation.\\n\\nIt allows existing `AuthenticationState`-based templates to continue working while providing access to authorization metadata in failed authorization scenarios.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Authorization State Storage\\n\\n`AuthorizeViewCore` should preserve the full authorization result internally.\\n\\nConceptually, instead of storing only whether authorization succeeded, the component stores:\\n\\n```csharp\\nprivate AuthorizationResult? currentAuthorizationResult;\\n```\\n\\nThe `null` state represents that authorization is still in progress.\\n\\nWhen no authorization data applies to the component, the result is treated as successful:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncurrentAuthorizationResult = AuthorizationResult.Success();\\n```\\n\\nWhen authorization data is present, the component stores the full result returned by the authorization service:\\n\\n```csharp\\ncurrentAuthorizationResult =\\n    await AuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(\\n        user,\\n        Resource,\\n        policy);\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Existing Fragments\\n\\nThe existing fragments remain:\\n\\n```csharp\\nRenderFragment? ChildContent\\nRenderFragment? Authorized\\nRenderFragment? NotAuthorized\\nRenderFragment? Authorizing\\n```\\n\\n### New Fragment\\n\\nAdd:\\n\\n```csharp\\nRenderFragment? Forbidden\\n```\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Rendering Behavior\\n\\nThe conceptual rendering behavior is:\\n\\n```csharp\\nif (authorizationResult is null)\\n{\\n    render Authorizing;\\n}\\nelse if (authorizationResult.Succeeded)\\n{\\n    render Authorized or ChildContent with AuthenticationState;\\n}\\nelse\\n{\\n    var stateWithResult = new AuthorizationStateWithResult(\\n        currentAuthenticationState.User,\\n        authorizationResult);\\n\\n    if (currentAuthenticationState.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true \\u0026amp;\\u0026amp;\\n        Forbidden is not null)\\n    {\\n        render Forbidden with stateWithResult;\\n    }\\n    else\\n    {\\n        render NotAuthorized with stateWithResult;\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\nThis means:\\n\\n- `Forbidden` is preferred for authenticated failed authorization.\\n- `NotAuthorized` remains the fallback path.\\n- Both failed authorization paths can access the full `AuthorizationResult`.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### Rendering Matrix\\n\\n| Scenario | Rendered Fragment | Context Type |\\n|---|---|---|...

Adds a comment to an existing GitHub issue, pull request, or discussion. Use this to provide feedback, answer questions, or add information to an existing conversation. For creating new items, use create_issue, create_discussion, or create_pull_request instead. IMPORTANT: Comments are subject to validation constraints enforced by the MCP server - maximum 65536 characters for the complete comment (including footer which is added automatically), 10 mentions (@username), and 50 links. Exceeding these limits will result in an immediate error with specific guidance. NOTE: Discussion comments are disabled for this workflow because discussions:write permission is not available. Set 'discussions: true' in the workflow's safe-outputs.add-comment configuration to enable discussion comments and request this permission. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 comment(s) can be added. Target: *. This tool records a real comment intent. Do not use it for placeholder comments, auth checks, or probing. Call it only when the final comment body is ready; otherwise use noop or report_incomplete.

safeoutputs.description: Add labels to an existing GitHub issue or pull request for categorization and filtering. Labels must already exist in the repository. For creating new issues with labels, use create_issue with the labels property instead. CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 3 label(s) can be added. Only these labels are allowed: ["area-auth" "area-blazor" "area-commandlinetools" "area-dataprotection" "area-grpc" "area-healthchecks" "area-hosting" "area-identity" "area-infrastructure" "area-middleware" "area-minimal" "area-mvc" "area-networking" "area-perf" "area-routing" "area-security" "area-signalr" "area-ui-rendering" "area-unified-build" "by-design" "question" "external" "docs" "api-proposal" "test-failure" "performance"]. INTENT ENCOURAGED: Include rationale (string, max 280 chars) and confidence (exactly one of: LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH) with each call. These fields are optional but strongly encouraged — they improve transparency and should normally be included. Use suggest: true alongside rationale and confidence to route for human review.

safeoutputs.description: Remove labels from an existing GitHub issue or pull request. Silently skips labels that don't exist on the item. Use this to clean up labels or manage label lifecycles (e.g., removing 'needs-review' after review is complete). CONSTRAINTS: Maximum 1 label(s) can be removed. Only these labels can be removed: [needs-area-label].
safeoutputs.name: remove_labels

safeoutputs.description: Report that a tool or capability needed to complete the task is not available, or share any information you deem important about missing functionality or limitations. Use this when you cannot accomplish what was requested because the required functionality is missing or access is restricted. When a bash command is blocked by security policy, call this tool with reason set to "security".

safeoutputs.description: Log a transparency message when no significant actions are needed. Use this to confirm workflow completion and provide visibility when analysis is complete but no changes or outputs are required (e.g., 'No issues found', 'All checks passed'). safeoutputs.description: Signal that the task could not be completed due to an infrastructure or tool failure (e.g., MCP server crash, missing authentication, inaccessible repository). Use this when required tools or data are unavailable and the task cannot be meaningfully performed. This is distinct from noop (no action needed) — it indicates an active failure that prevented the task from running. Provide a specific reason and optional details so downstream issue aggregation can preserve complete incomplete-signal context.
